referents.why: First person 'my' in 'my feet' (morph first/common/singular). In a psalm this is the psalm's own voice, but the candidate list offers no voice candidate, so no candidate id can be chosen.
referents.category: psalm voice with no voice candidate

referents.why: Second person masculine singular 'your' in 'your word'; the psalm addresses God in prayer. The only masculine singular divine-name candidate is LORD (Psa.119.89#w0).
referents.category: second person address to God in psalm prayer

referents.why: First person 'my' in 'my path' (morph first/common/singular): the psalm's own voice, which is not among the candidates.
referents.category: psalm voice with no voice candidate

links.why: The waw joins two parallel predications with the same subject 'your word' (a lamp to my feet / a light to my path). The sense is restatement, not cause, result or purpose, so plain 'and' stands.

groups.why: The second line 'a light to my path' restates the first's roles ('to my ...') without its subject, which is the same word 'your word'. This is the parallel kind, recorded as a new group for review.

cant_tell.what: Slots w3 (my feet) and w10 (my path): the psalm's own voice
cant_tell.why: The rule makes the first person the psalm's voice, but no voice candidate is listed, so the referent cannot be chosen from the candidates.
